components.explanation: Effect A and the event it rides on. Three GPUParticles2D under one Node2D - Flash owns frame one, Grit owns the shape, Dust owns the tail - plus the spike trap whose `fired` signal already existed and was not changed, and the spawner that instances one burst per event rather than reusing a node. The retrigger rule is overlap, which is what stops the second of two close events being silently dropped on a one_shot emitter.

Effect B: ambience, one emitter, sixty motes, no event. Its condition is the scene being loaded with the player alive and it stops on `died`. The feature Effect A does not use is `preprocess = 8.0`, one full lifetime simulated before the first frame is drawn - the one rule in this assignment that no headless run in this repository can see.

Effect C: dust under the feet, on an event this game does not have. `player.gd` has a position, a velocity and a floor check and no footstep signal, so the driver derives the event from distance travelled on the ground - one puff per 24 px, back-dated by the overshoot so the spacing is the same at any frame rate. It is also the only effect that uses `amount_ratio`, 0.6 for a stride against 1.0 for a landing.

Godot's own particle process shader, produced by converting Effect A's Dust material in the editor. Nothing in the game loads it; it is in the project to be read. Dust is the emitter that was converted because it is the only one carrying both a colour ramp and a scale curve, and the two lines that sample them only exist in a generated shader when the material actually has them. The scratch scene holds the verbatim copy of the material that was converted.

What the effects are attached to and what drives them in play: the three-trap room, the player who can only walk and jump, the backdrop and audio the contrast decisions were judged against, the pose driver and warning driver that already kept the read-never-write boundary, the F9 vsync key this assignment added, and the project settings that pin the renderer and the logical resolution.

What the price claims and the footage rest on. The cost script that runs the assignment's four named conditions with an empty-scene control and a twice-run baseline, so it states its own noise floor before reporting any difference; its windowed sibling, which reads GPU time off the same timestamp query the editor's Visual Profiler displays and refuses to run headless, because a dummy renderer would report 0.000 ms for every condition and look like three effects that cost nothing; the capture driver that records all three takes and asserts its own outcome before a frame of it counts as evidence; and the input-map check, which is how the F9 key is shown to have added no action.

code_result_pairs.observation: C1 RESULT. take-p, PLAYED: held keys through the real input map, nothing teleported. The take asserts three traps fired, four bursts and twenty five step-dust puffs before a frame of it counts.

Effect A's tuning revision 6.0.1, with the author's verdict. Fixture capture from godot/previews/hit_burst_preview.tscn, labelled. The per-frame difference counts are recomputed from the committed frames at build time by scripts/compose_particles_evidence.py.

F4 demonstrated by mutation: the same preview with preprocess set to 0.0 in the scene file and reverted immediately after. Both are FIXTURE captures. Mote pixels are recomputed at build time from the committed frames against frame 340 of the shipped run, which is the same field eight seconds after it stopped - an empty room.

The two shader lines beside the brief settings they implement, with the engine output those settings produce. Frames 15 and 20 of the kept r1 capture - FIXTURE - where Dust is the only emitter still alive. The deltas are recomputed at build time.
C5 RESULT. take-p again, the feet. Played: held keys only. The run east and the run west are in one unbroken take, so the mirror is visible rather than claimed.

The recorded output of scripts/run-test.sh cost_effects.gd 60 300, drawn verbatim at build time from evidence/a6/cost-effects.txt, above a frame of take-r with three bursts alive. The GPU budgets are NOT settled by this script and the card says so.
